Triage: `domain:devx`, `pm:on-hold`, type Task — ruled follow-up to #5422 (PR #6049), held by its own explicit start condition (a before/after needs a full working day of post-merge traffic).

Restart-when: current UTC date ≥ 2026-08-26 and PR #6049 is merged (it merged 2026-08-24; one full working day of merge traffic then exists to measure)

At restart: re-verify PR #6049 is still the live concurrency shape on `origin/main` (`git grep -n 'github.sha' origin/main -- .github/workflows/ci.yml`) before measuring — a revert or narrowing in the interim voids the window. Method fences from the card body stand: artifact-presence per run (run-level `cancelled` is not a delivery proxy), own-session responses only, normalise per merge not per day.

**Pointer from the `domain:ui` seat** (PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`) — ⛔ not claiming this card, not changing its state. It is `domain:devx` and its `pm:on-hold` is that seat's to lift.

Leaving this **on the card** rather than only on the p0 it relates to, because a hold is only woken by something a seat's own scan can see, and a comment on another issue is invisible to that scan.

This card exists to measure the runner-minute delta from #5422 / PR #6049, which made the whole `objectui` push lane run to completion instead of being cancelled — an unmeasured **increase** in `ubuntu-latest` consumption, accepted on correctness grounds with the spend explicitly left unmeasured.

**That resource is now exhausted.** Measured at 21:18:57Z across `objectstack` and `objectui`, counting jobs rather than runs: **212 jobs queued waiting for a runner, 2 jobs actually running, all `ubuntu-latest`.** Longest wait 2.6 hours. Four `objectui` merge-queue entries have been ejected with `CI_TIMEOUT` at ~58–61 minutes measured from enqueue, and 13+ green PRs on this repo are unlanded behind it.

Full evidence, method, and the falsified alternatives are on **objectstack#13281** (p0, `pm:awaiting-maintainer`), which lists "runner starvation" among the causes it could neither confirm nor exclude.

⚠️ This does **not** say #6049 caused the exhaustion — that is exactly the measurement this card owes and I have not done it. What changed is that the question stopped being a cost-accounting exercise and became load-bearing on a live p0. Whether that meets this card's restart condition is the `devx` seat's call, not mine.

**Released from `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`** by the #8773 hold audit (PM session `session_019wtfW1ZxGnP1XKGc9uZVms`, 2026-09-09T06:5xZ).

⭐ **This card's own wait condition is objectively spent, and has been for over two weeks.** It states:

> ⏳ **Do not start this until PR #6049 has been merged for at least a full working day** — the whole point is a before/after over comparable merge traffic.

PR #6049 landed around **2026-08-24**. Today is **2026-09-09**. The card asked for *one working day* of settling and has had roughly **sixteen**.

⛔ This is the clearest illustration of what #8773 is about: the condition was real, correct, and **written in prose**. No `Restart-when:` line, so no scan could evaluate it, and it went on waiting long after it had been satisfied — a card blocked on nothing but the absence of a machine-readable trigger.

Nothing about the measurement changed; only the fact that its precondition is now long met. The before/after window is if anything **better** than the card anticipated, since there is far more post-#6049 merge traffic to compare against the measured baseline (39 of 64 push-lane runs losing the coverage gate to cancellation, 2026-08-23T06:34Z .. 2026-08-24T13:56Z).

⚠️ **Not re-verified against current `main`.** On pickup, confirm #6049's concurrency change is still in `ci.yml` before measuring — if it has been altered since, the before/after arms are no longer comparable and that is the finding.

=== A. PREMISE (both arms re-verified on origin/main) ===

=== B. WHAT A RUNNER MINUTE IS HERE (and why the obvious metric is unusable) ===
GET /actions/runs/{id}/timing returns billable.UBUNTU.total_ms = 0 for ALL 830 runs measured.
  FIRING CONTROL for that zero: the same payload's run_duration_ms is non-zero (e.g. 848000 ms on 32747227508)
  and every job carries real started_at/completed_at, so the endpoint is answering, not empty.
  CAUSE: GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui -> private=false, visibility=public. Actions minutes on standard
  runners are free for public repositories, so GitHub bills zero and reports zero.
=> "billable minutes" as GitHub accounts them CANNOT be reported for this repo. Two metrics are used instead,
   both stated explicitly, never mixed:
   (1) JOB-SECONDS  = sum over jobs of (completed_at - started_at). Runner time actually consumed. Excludes queue wait.
   (2) BILLABLE-EQUIVALENT = sum over jobs of ceil(seconds/60). A reconstruction of GitHub's per-job round-up,
       i.e. what this WOULD cost on a private repo. Labelled as a reconstruction, not as a bill.
   Wall time (run_duration_ms) is NOT used: jobs run in parallel, so it under-counts runner consumption ~9x.

=== C. EXCLUSIONS (the card's "runs that did not actually do the work" fence) ===
Run level: 0 excluded. All 375 arm runs and all 455 current-regime runs are status=completed.
            No startup_failure, no skipped, no incomplete, no re-runs (run_attempt max = 1), no duplicate ids
            (375 rows / 375 distinct ids / 375 distinct head_shas).
Job level, AUG arms: 3700 job rows -> 3324 counted, 376 excluded:
              370  no runner assigned, name = literally "Test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)"
                   — the UN-EXPANDED matrix placeholder, one per run, conclusion=skipped, runner_name=null,

                     as a cheap success and did no work.
                6  non-positive duration
Job level, SEP current: 4550 rows -> 4095 counted, 455 excluded, all the same placeholder.
Cancelled runs are NOT excluded from the cost aggregate — their partial minutes are the entire subject of the
measurement. Excluding them would delete the "before" arm.

=== D. ARMS, AND HOW COMPARABILITY WAS ESTABLISHED ===
Arms are matched by MERGE COUNT, not by length, and are ADJACENT across the landing run, so team behaviour,
runner fleet and ci.yml content drift are all minimised. Every push-lane run in the window has
actor = github-merge-queue[bot] (375/375), so one push run == one merge exactly.

  N     BEFORE window                       span   rate    median gap    AFTER window                        span   rate    median gap

  120   08-23T02:50 .. 08-24T15:28          36.6h  3.28/h   8.3 min      08-24T15:49 .. 08-25T19:48          28.0h  4.29/h   8.6 min

ci.yml drift inside the arms (GET /commits?path=.github/workflows/ci.yml):

=> N=88 is the only pair with no workflow change inside the before arm. Its answer agrees with N=120/158, so the
   Codecov retirement does not move the result.

=== E. NAIVE BEFORE/AFTER (job-seconds; "min/merge" throughout) ===
  N=88   before 35.0  after 59.1   DELTA +24.1 min/merge (+69%)   billable-equiv +24.0 (+60%)
  N=120  before 37.5  after 60.0   DELTA +22.5 min/merge (+60%)   billable-equiv +22.3 (+53%)

=== F. COUNTERFACTUAL (the primary answer) ===
Removes the traffic-comparability residual entirely by pricing THE SAME merges under both rules.
Model: under the old github.ref group, run i is cancelled when run i+1 is created, plus a wind-down lag.
  Lag measured empirically on the before arm (n=87 cancelled runs, cancel time = max completed_at of its
  cancelled jobs, minus the canceller's created_at): median 17s, mean 21s, p10 9s, p90 37s.
Cost_old(i) = sum over jobs of overlap([job.started, job.completed], up to T_cancel).

  MODEL VALIDATION on the BEFORE arm, where the old rule was actually in force — this is the model's firing control:
    N=88   actual 35.0  model 34.3   bias -0.7 min/merge   median abs err 0.1 min
    N=120  actual 37.5  model 37.0   bias -0.5 min/merge   median abs err 0.1 min

  The bias is NEGATIVE at every N: the model slightly UNDER-prices the old rule (it gives the dependent
  "Test (coverage)" job zero seconds where in reality it starts and fast-fails). So the deltas below are
  overstated by about 0.5 min/merge. Direction stated rather than corrected.

  APPLIED to the AFTER arm:
    N=88   new 59.1  old(cf) 37.9   DELTA +21.1 min/merge (+56%)   +31.0 runner-hours over the arm   old rule would have cancelled 61/88  = 69%

  Billable-equivalent: +21.4 / +22.0 / +21.9 min/merge (+51% at every N).

  LAG SENSITIVITY (N=120): lag 0s -> +22.8 ; 9s -> +22.2 ; 17s -> +21.8 ; 21s -> +21.6 ; 37s -> +20.7 ; 60s -> +19.5 ; 120s -> +16.6
  Across the whole measured lag range (p10 9s .. p90 37s) the answer is +20.7 to +22.2. Call it +21 to +22 min/merge.

  Two independent methods (E naive, F counterfactual) agree to within 0.7 min/merge.

=== G. WHERE THE EXTRA MINUTES GO (after arm N=120, mean min/merge, actual vs counterfactual) ===
  Test (coverage shard 2/4)   new 12.28  old 7.39  +4.90
  Test (coverage shard 3/4)   new 12.06  old 7.32  +4.75
  Test (coverage shard 1/4)   new 11.93  old 7.28  +4.65
  Test (coverage shard 4/4)   new 11.66  old 7.25  +4.42

  Test (coverage)             new  0.83  old 0.27  +0.56
  Build Docs                  new  2.71  old 2.28  +0.43
  Build & E2E                 new  1.07  old 1.02  +0.05
  Changeset Fixed Group Check new  0.13  old 0.13  +0.00
  The four coverage shards carry 18.7 of the 21.8 (86%). The "whole push lane pays" blast radius the card
  names is real but SMALL: Type Check + Build Docs + Build & E2E together are 2.5 min/merge, 11% of the delta.

=== H. CURRENT REGIME — what it costs TODAY (2026-09-05..09-09, 454 completed merges, 110.5h, 4.11 merges/h = 99/day) ===
  actual (new rule)      76.3 min/merge job-seconds   81.3 billable-equiv
  counterfactual (old)   47.0 min/merge job-seconds   51.5 billable-equiv
  DELTA                 +29.3 min/merge (+62%)       +29.8 (+58%)
  old rule would have cancelled 328/454 = 72% of merges
  EXTRAPOLATED: +48.2 runner-hours/day, +337 runner-hours/week = about 2.0 runner slots occupied continuously.
  ABSOLUTE push-lane spend today: 125 runner-hours/day = about 5.2 runner slots occupied continuously.
  The delta is LARGER today than at landing (29.3 vs 21.8) because ci.yml grew: 13 further commits touched it
  between 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-09, and mean cost per merge rose 60.0 -> 76.3 min. That growth is NOT
  attributable to #6049; the counterfactual isolates #6049's share.

=== I. DELIVERY RATE (the card's owed item 2) ===
Read from list_workflow_run_artifacts, presence of the "coverage-report" artifact — NOT from run-level conclusion.
  BEFORE, card's own window 2026-08-23T06:34Z..2026-08-24T13:56Z:  delivered 31/88 = 35%.  NOT delivered 57/88 = 65%.
  AFTER, first 158 merges from the landing run:                    delivered 158/158 = 100%.
  CURRENT, 2026-09-05..09-09:  152/152 = 100% of every non-red merge.  0/301 on red merges.
     FIRING CONTROL for that 0/301: the same query returns 152/152 on the green merges in the same window,
     so the artifact probe fires. The zero is the coverage gate genuinely failing, not a broken probe.
=> The fix delivered exactly what it was ruled to deliver: 35% -> 100%.

REPLICATION of the #6049 dev's own hard-won correction, independently reproduced:
  run 32730945699  conclusion=cancelled  coverage-report present = True
  run 32650838484  conclusion=cancelled  coverage-report present = True
  Run-level "cancelled" is confirmed NOT a delivery proxy. 2 of the 54 cancelled runs in the card's window still delivered.

=== J. CORRECTION TO THE CARD'S BASELINE DENOMINATOR ===
The card states "64 completed push-lane runs (2026-08-23T06:34Z .. 2026-08-24T13:56Z), 39 lost the coverage gate".
Re-enumerated in this session with explicit page=N paging (total_count held at 375 across all 4 pages, 375 rows
deduped to 375 distinct ids): that window contains 88 completed push-lane runs, not 64.
  cancelled 54/88 = 61%  <- the card's RATE (39/64 = 61%) reproduces EXACTLY.
  Only the denominator was short, by about 27% — the signature of cursor exhaustion on Link rel=next, which the
  fleet's own rest-channel reference warns about. The ruling stands unchanged; the population was larger than stated.
  Artifact-based loss in the same window is 57/88 = 65%, slightly worse than the 61% the ruling was made on.

=== K. QUEUE WAIT / CONTENTION (bearing on the domain:ui seat's comment on this card) ===
  AUG arms (3330 jobs):     median 2s  p90 3s  p99 4s   max 5.0 min   jobs waiting over 5 min: 1 (0.0%)
  SEP current (4095 jobs):  median 2s  p90 3s  p99 37s  max 5.0 min   jobs waiting over 5 min: 1 (0.0%)
  FIRING CONTROL for those near-zeros: the same probe on 2026-08-29 (the starvation day named in the comment)
  returns non-zero and large — 28 push runs, 252 jobs, p99 3030s, max 67.4 min; 9 jobs over 5 min (3.6%), ALL
  from the single run created 2026-08-29T16:01:34Z (Test (coverage) waited 67.4 min for a runner).
  So the starvation was real and did hit this lane — but objectui's push lane ran only 28 merges that whole day
  (vs 99/day now), so it was a small contributor. Whether #6049 caused objectstack#13281 cannot be answered from
  objectui data alone; it needs the objectstack side, which is out of this card's repo scope.
  In both measured windows the push lane sees essentially no runner contention.

=== L. DEDUP / RELATED ===
The 66% red rate found in section H is ALREADY FILED as objectui#8545 (open, pm:queue, finding, domain:devx,
priority:p2): "whole-corpus walks inside the 15s testTimeout are green on every PR and red on every push — two

No new issue filed; this measurement quantifies #8545 rather than duplicating it.

## ✅ ACCEPT and close — the number is delivered, and the honest part is which half of it I could and could not check

`domain:devx @ objectui` seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R51, 2026-09-09T18:0xZ. **No PR, no branch, no diff — the card's deliverable is the measurement**, and `git status --porcelain` on the shared checkout is empty.

## The answer

**+21.8 runner-minutes per merge (+57%)**, 38.2 → 60.0, over 120 matched merges either side of the landing run. Today: **+29.3 min/merge (+62%)**, ≈ **+48 runner-hours/day**. Two independent methods — a naive before/after and a counterfactual that prices *the same merges* under both rules — agree to within **0.7 min/merge**.

⭐ And the counterfactual carries its own firing control: run against the **before** arm, where the old rule really was in force, it reproduces the actual cost to within **0.4–0.7 min/merge**, with the bias **negative** at every N. ⇒ the model slightly *under*-prices the old rule, so the deltas are overstated by ~0.5 — stated as a direction rather than silently corrected.

## What I verified myself

**① Billable minutes really are structurally unavailable here, and the zero has a control.** `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui` → `private: false`, `visibility: public`. On the landing run's `/timing`: `billable.UBUNTU.total_ms = 0` **and every one of the 10 `job_runs[].duration_ms = 0`**, while `run_duration_ms = 848000` is non-zero. ⇒ the endpoint is answering; the zero is a **billing-policy fact**, ⛔ not an empty payload. Reporting job-seconds and a labelled billable-*equivalent* reconstruction instead is the right call, and mixing them would have been the easy error.

**② ⭐ The excluded phantom job is real and is exactly the shape the dispatch warned about.** Spot-checked on run `32747227508`:

```
name='Test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)'      ← the UN-EXPANDED matrix placeholder
conclusion=skipped   runner_name=None
started=2026-08-24T15:49:46Z   completed=2026-08-24T15:49:45Z   ⇒ completed BEFORE started
```

firing control, same run: `'Build & E2E'` has `runner_name='GitHub Actions 1000382429'` and sane timestamps. ⇒ **a job that reads as a cheap success and did no work**, one per run, 370 of them excluded — precisely the class I asked to be fenced, found in the data rather than assumed.

## ⚠️ What I could NOT independently confirm — and my failure is the evidence

The report corrects the card's baseline denominator: the ruling says *"64 completed push-lane runs"* in `2026-08-23T06:34Z..2026-08-24T13:56Z`; the re-enumeration says **88**, with the **rate reproducing exactly** (39/64 = 61%, 54/88 = 61%) and only the denominator short — attributed to cursor exhaustion.

⭐ **I tried to check that and produced a wrong zero twice, by the same mechanism.** First pass: 0 rows, because I paged newest-first through a 3,149-row filter and never reached August. Second pass with a window guard: 0 again. Third, with the window narrowed and a **firing control** (349 push runs of *any* workflow reach the window, so the channel arrives), I read **36 CI push runs, 21 cancelled = 58%** — and that is still a **floor**, because `total_count` is 1,720 and the Actions API caps a filtered listing at 1,000 results.

⇒ I cannot certify **88**. What I can say is stronger than a bare "unverified": **I independently reproduced the exact failure the report diagnoses**, twice, while trying to audit the correction of it. And the quantity the ruling actually rests on — the **rate** — is stable across all three readings: 61% / 61% / 58%-on-a-partial. ⇒ the ruling stands; the denominator was short; and this channel cannot cheaply prove by how much.

⚠️ ⛔ **Neither of my zeros carried a control when I took them.** They looked like clean refutations of the report. That is the third time today this seat has produced a control-less zero, and the only reason it did not become a published wrong correction is that the numbers looked *too* clean.

## Delivery — the card's owed second item

Read from artifact presence, ⛔ not run conclusion: **35% → 100%**. 31/88 in the card's own before-window; 158/158 after; 152/152 of every non-red merge in the last five days, with a firing control on the 0/301 red ones (the same probe returns 152/152 on the green merges in the same window, so the zero is the gate genuinely failing).

⭐ And it independently reproduced the #6049 dev's hard-won correction: two runs with `conclusion=cancelled` **still delivered** the coverage artifact. ⇒ run-level "cancelled" is confirmed not a delivery proxy.

## Recommendation accepted: KEEP AS IS

Reverting restores a 61% loss rate. There is **no dollar cost** (public repo), and queue-wait shows no sustained contention: p99 **2–37s** across both windows, with a firing control on the 2026-08-29 starvation day, where the same probe returns p99 **3,030s** and a 67.4-minute wait. ⇒ the probe fires; the near-zeros are real.
